name: Into Another
label: Revelation
lede: A Youth of Today singer, a Bold drummer and a thrash bassist made hard rock with a Wurlitzer in it, and the hardcore kids stagedived anyway, right up until a major label shipped their album with somebody else's music on the disc.

eras.title: Out of the box on the Lower East Side
eras.text: Richie Birkenhead and Drew Thomas came from the heart of youth crew hardcore and wanted no part of its rules. They found a guitarist who could really play and a bassist from a thrash band, and set about making something nobody in the matinee crowd had asked for.

q: We were unbelievably surprised that we were embraced to the degree that we were.
years.h: Richie Birkenhead and Drew Thomas start Into Another
years.p: Richie Birkenhead ([[Underdog|de38fbd3-7155-497a-bf3c-1a8db3091859]], [[Youth of Today|9ca27db4-f127-4aeb-ae87-29e21f558c13]]) and Drew Thomas ([[Bold|b024b1bd-2020-4b7c-83f7-4660133c89fa]], [[Crippled Youth|ad695a64-ac47-4320-a0c2-3aa7a4c5abc4]]) recruit guitarist Peter Moses and bassist [[Tony Bono|7ca7aa95-78a3-4330-9fac-390d6dfc6646]], late of the thrash band Whiplash. The plan is to belong to no genre at all.
years.xp:
Birkenhead has said he and Thomas joked about alienating people and wanted to get free of having to conform to anything. What they got instead was a scene that followed them.

Revelation's own bio pins down the sound: one foot in the New York hardcore family, the other fishing through classic rock.

years.p: The debut LP on Revelation, the label behind Youth of Today and Bold, Richie Birkenhead's and Drew Thomas's old bands. It sounds like neither of them.

eras.title: The buzz band
eras.text: The records got stranger and the crowds got bigger. By Ignaurus, Into Another was named alongside Quicksand and Orange 9mm as the New York hardcore alumni the rock world was watching.

years.p: The bridge between Into Another and Ignaurus, on Revelation, with Richie Birkenhead, Peter Moses, Tony Bono and Drew Thomas still intact.

The album that makes Into Another a buzz band: hard rock, alt-rock, grunge and post-hardcore in a single record that somehow doesn't fall apart. On the West Coast, the Sloth Crew kids are stagediving to it.

eras.title: The Hollywood mistake
eras.text: The major-label deal should have been the payoff: a producer with a Pearl Jam record on his résumé and a single on rock radio. Instead it became a case study in how a label can sink a band, and it ended Into Another.

years.p: Into Another's last Revelation releases of the original run.

years.h: Into Another signs to Hollywood Records
years.p: The Disney-owned label pairs Into Another with [[Rick Parashar|ad1ea089-1b0a-454c-bb29-c5477d612137]], who produced Pearl Jam's Ten.

years.h: Seemless: three weeks in Seattle and New York
years.p: Into Another's Hollywood album is cut at London Bridge Studios in Seattle plus Shelter Island and Sorcerer Sound in New York. Richie Birkenhead plays Wurlitzer, Drew Thomas adds congas, and Victor Axelrod sits in on Hammond B3.

years.big: The single charted. The album wasn't in stores.
years.h: Hollywood ships Seemless with the wrong music on the disc
years.p: Richie Birkenhead's account: copies of Seemless shipped to some regions with another band's music on the CD, and the Mutate Me video aired with its volume turned down.
years.xp:
By Birkenhead's telling, T.A.I.L. was on rock radio while the album couldn't be found. He blames terrible distribution and promotion, and says Hollywood breached the contract repeatedly.

When the band talked about suing, the label threatened litigation without end. Into Another took a settlement far below what the contract was worth. For years afterward the album was deleted and missing from digital stores.

years.p: Noah Bogen directs the video for the Seemless single. The song reaches No. 39 on Billboard's Mainstream Rock Tracks.

years.h: Hollywood shelves Soul Control, and Into Another splits
years.p: A final, electronica-leaning album, Soul Control, is recorded for Hollywood and never released. Worn down by internal conflict and the label, Into Another splits the same year.

eras.title: The glue
eras.text: Into Another had been over for years, but losing bassist Tony Bono closed a door that everyone had assumed would stay open a crack.

q: He was the backbone and the glue; he held it all together.
years.p: Blabbermouth reports Into Another's bassist died overnight after an apparent heart attack; he was playing in the hard rock trio FR8 at the time. Richie Birkenhead is in Los Angeles when he gets the news, and drives across the country for the funeral.
years.xp: Birkenhead has called Tony Bono the band's backbone and glue, and said he took that loss harder than any other he can remember. For a decade, it made a reunion feel impossible.

eras.title: Two younger players bring them back
eras.text: It took Revelation's anniversary, and two musicians who'd grown up on the records, to get Peter Moses out of retirement upstate. The reunion stuck, and eventually it made new music.

years.h: Into Another reunite for Revelation 25 in Pomona
years.p: Richie Birkenhead, Peter Moses and Drew Thomas return with [[Brian Balchack|62436915-6d04-4893-a4c4-e6b48d8a4dba]] and Reid Black for the label's 25th anniversary shows at The Glasshouse in Pomona, California.
The first new Into Another music in nearly two decades, from the reunited five-piece.

eras.title: Seemless, found
eras.text: The album that Hollywood buried finally surfaced where people listen now.

years.p: Nearly thirty years after it vanished from shelves, Into Another's 1995 Hollywood Records album is on the major streaming services.
